title: Petra and the Winter
premise: Casper Sandoval takes a teaching post in the snowbound town of Vesper Hollow, where a classroom of children vanished decades ago and the town has quietly agreed never to count them again. Moving into the old Sandoval house she inherited from a grandmother she never met, Casper discovers the mirrors lag one second behind reality — and in that stolen second, the missing class is still taking attendance. The house demands an heir join the roll before winter's end; her only ally is Petra, the caretaker's daughter who once escaped being counted and now remembers nothing but the cold. To break the inheritance, Casper must let herself be counted and answer 'absent' at the final roll call — unmaking her claim to the house and nearly her own identity — while Petra holds her hand and speaks her true name to pull her back. The class is released, the mirrors go still, and Casper, no longer a Sandoval by anything but choice, stays in Vesper Hollow with Petra as spring thaws.
about_author: Zephyrine Nakamura is a former substitute teacher who spent one strange winter in a northern mill town and never quite stopped listening for roll calls. She writes horror about houses that remember people better than people do.

chapters.title: Attendance
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Arriving in Vesper Hollow during the first snowfall, Casper inherits the shuttered Sandoval house and a classroom roster with thirteen names crossed out. Her students whisper about the missing class; the principal warns her never to take attendance aloud. In the hallway mirror, her reflection blinks after she does. Emotional beat: unease dressed up as fresh starts — the thrill of belonging curdling into the sense of being expected.

chapters.title: The Second Behind the Glass
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Every mirror in the house now lags a full second, and in that gap Casper sees children seated at desks, turning toward her. Petra, the caretaker's quiet daughter, recognizes the faces from a photograph and fragments return: she was meant to be the fourteenth. The house begins rearranging itself around Casper — her handwriting appearing on old homework, her name inked into the roster. Emotional beat: dread deepening into complicity as Casper realizes the inheritance is claiming her.

chapters.title: Roll Call at Midnight
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Casper and Petra. On the winter solstice the house seals its doors and the mirrors open fully; the missing class files out to hold attendance, and the house requires its heir to answer. Casper chooses to stand and be counted so the roll can be broken from inside, while Petra fights through the frozen halls, armed with the one thing the house can't keep — Casper's spoken name. Climax: at the final call, Casper answers 'absent,' and the room tries to erase her. Emotional beat: love against duty, sacrifice offered freely.

chapters.title: Spring Thaw
chapters.summary: POV: Petra, closing on Casper. Petra's voice drags Casper back across the threshold as the mirrors shatter inward and thirteen children walk out into the snow, finally dismissed. The house goes cold and ordinary; the Sandoval name dissolves from the deed and from Casper's memory of why she ever owed it anything. She wakes with no inheritance left but her own name, given back to her by Petra's mouth. Emotional beat: release and chosen belonging — identity rebuilt not from blood, but from being known.
